# `charset`

Byte-order mark handling. Not set, a file keeps whatever mark it arrived with.

## Values

| Value | Notes |
|---|---|
| `utf-8` |  |
| `utf-8-bom` |  |

**Default:** `(not set)`

## Conformance

No known case where Curb's output is not a fixed point of `dotnet format` — see [conformance](../../design-principles/conformance.md).

## Effect

`utf-8` writes the file without a byte-order mark and `utf-8-bom` writes it with one. Curb reads and writes UTF-8 either way, so a code block can't show the difference. With the key unset, each file keeps the mark it arrived with. The other EditorConfig values (`latin1`, `utf-16be`, `utf-16le`) are reported as unrecognised, since re-encoding a file is not a formatting change.
